newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Beijing Enterprises grabs centre stage in HK.
newsitem.headline: Beijing Enterprises grabs centre stage in HK.

text.p: China's latest red chip stock burst into action on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on Thursday, more than trebling in price at the opening bell while the rest of the market was left in the dust.

Days of anticipation over Beijing Enterprises Holdings Ltd's stock market debut unleashed a mad scramble for its shares, which skyrocketed to HK$41.00 (US$5.30) in opening trade as traders on the market floor cheered.
"It reflects people's confidence in Hong Kong after the handover," Beijing Enterprises chairman Hu Zhao Guang told traders at the company's listing ceremony on Thursday.

The red chip conglomerate, controlled by Beijing's municipal government, launched a 150 million share global initial public offering last week at HK$12.48 a share amid an investor craze for China plays ahead of Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule.
The British colony will be handed over to China at midnight on June 30.
The portion of 13.5 million shares offered to the Hong Kong public was 1,276 times subscribed, the highest subscription level ever in the territory.
Francis Leung, chairman of Peregrine Capital, said the flood of applications tied up about HK$215 billion in Hong Kong's banking system.
Beijing Enteprises also offered 135 million shares to international investors and 1.5 million to its employees.
The company's connections to the Chinese capital have fuelled a huge appetite for its shares in Hong Kong.
It is 69 percent owned by Beijing Holdings Ltd, the primary trading and commercial vehicle in Hong Kong of the Beijing municipal government. Hu is vice-mayor of Beijing.
"We will make an effort to maintain the political and economic development of Hong Kong and China," Hu said.
Shares in Beijing Enterprises reached a high of HK$45.00 before settling to trade around HK$40.90.
Meanwhile, the Hang Seng blue-chip index was down 212 points, or 1.46 percent, at 14,342 in late-morning trade.
"Nobody cares about blue chips today. Most of the blue chips are down," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at BNP PrimeEast Securities.
He said many investors had been tempted to take profits in Beijing Enterprises shares during the first minutes of trade.

Most applications for the offering were for 6,000 shares or less. Investors who sold their 6,000 shares at the opening were likely to have pocketed more than HK$140,000 after transaction costs, said Tsang.
But brokers said few clients had been tempted to place orders for Beijing Enteprises shares prior to the opening of trade on Thursday.
"We have a few orders but people are going to wait for the open," Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at NAVA SC Securities, said before the opening bell.
The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong said its members reported off-system trades between 9:00 am (0100 GMT) and 10:00 am for 90,000 shares worth HK$3.45 million.
Volume in Beijing Enterprises was a huge 44.79 million shares by midday, propelling overall volume on the stock exchange to HK$9.785 billion.
